emails.subject: A client project across 16 weeks
emails.single_idea: A substantial client project can be given a defined place on paper: 16 weeks of undated planning, supported by goal breakdowns and monthly, weekly and daily pages.
emails.selection_reason: The bounded 16-week format directly matches this reader’s selected planning horizon, while goal breakdowns and multiple planning views give a freelancer concrete details to evaluate for a client project without requiring trust in an unproven outcome.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the planner’s 16-week, undated structure and monthly, weekly and daily pages fit the reader’s client-project planning style.
emails.next_step_value: The product page’s documented “Look inside” action lets the reader inspect the planner while evaluating its monthly, weekly and daily planning format.
emails.next_step_limit: Looking inside does not establish a continuous rolling calendar, links between notes and dates, digital compatibility or whether using the planner will improve project results.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: A physical, undated 16-week spiral planner for shaping a client project into goals and monthly, weekly and daily handwritten plans away from screens.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The profile explicitly establishes that I am a freelancer delivering a client project, beginning a focused 16-week push and wanting to plan away from screens, so the core premise is unusually direct. The email additionally assumes that goal breakdowns and separate monthly, weekly and daily views suit how I work; that is plausible but not established. Whether I need a continuous rolling view or help resuming after missed weeks remains unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I am delivering a client project during a focused 16-week push.
Profile-supported: I want to do planning away from screens.
Email-only: the project is substantial enough to need its own dedicated planner.
Email-only: goal breakdowns will usefully shape the project before scheduling it.
Email-only: monthly, weekly and daily planning horizons fit how I want to organise the work.
reader_verdicts.problem_now: Organising the client project over the coming 16 weeks matters now because that focused push is explicitly established. A fragmented month-by-month view and difficulty resuming after missed weeks are plausible risks from the observed market context, but their applicability to me is not established.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: I cannot yet tell whether the month-divided pages preserve a useful continuous view of the full 16-week project or fragment it into separate calendar blocks. The Look inside view is an appropriate way to answer that ordinary layout question.
reader_verdicts.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me that the Look inside view clearly shows how the full 16-week span connects to the monthly, weekly and daily pages.
fixes: Rewrite "If a substantial client project needs a defined place away from screens, 16 weeks offers a clear frame for deciding what belongs within it." as "If you are mapping one client project across a focused 16-week push, this planner gives that work a dedicated place away from screens."

Rewrite "Monthly, weekly and daily planning pages then let you consider the project at different horizons — from its wider arc to the work for a given day." as "Monthly, weekly and daily pages show the available planning horizons; use Look inside to judge whether those separate views keep the full 16-week project connected enough for you."

Rewrite "The product page’s Look inside view lets you flick through the planner and inspect those formats before deciding whether they fit the way you want to organise the project." as "Open Look inside to inspect the goal, monthly, weekly and daily spreads before deciding whether the layout fits your project."

brief.promise: Papier offers freelancers a bounded paper structure for organising a client project across 16 undated weeks, from goal breakdowns to monthly, weekly and daily planning.
brief.orientation: A paper productivity planner for an individual professional organising daily work toward a substantial goal over a focused 16-week period.
brief.arc: In one standalone email, move from the concrete 16-week project-planning mechanism to a low-friction invitation to inspect the pages and judge the format personally.
brief.sequence_rationale: A single-email contract requires one complete argument. Lead with the documented 16-week mechanism because it directly matches the selected planning horizon, then support it with goal breakdowns and monthly, weekly and daily pages. The selected audience’s researched rolling-calendar problem is only partially matched, so it should not become the promise. The email should invite inspection rather than rely on absent customer proof or claim an outcome.
